text.p: Malaysian rubber prices continued their free fall to end lower in a market void of buyers, traders said.

At the close, the benchmark April RSS1 buyer was quoted at 303 cents ($1.23) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB), down 1.50 cents from Tuesday's close. April SMR20 buyer also ended 1.50 cents down at 289.50 cents.
Traders offered the SMR20 at 291 cents a kg, SMR CV at 355, SMR L at 335, SMR 5 at 207, SMR 10 at 292 and latex at 231.
They said producers were trying hard to match the low prices in Indonesia but were hampered by the high costs in Malaysia.
"The wintering season now has taken some pressure off stocks, otherwise rubber factories will have no space for new stocks," said a trader.
Wintering is the process where rubber trees shed their leaves and produce less latex.
The INRO five-day average was at 231.74 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on March 18 from 232.13 March 17. The daily indicator was at 230.41 from 231.77 previously.
